title: Innovation vs indication
html: Innovation has consistently been a hallmark of endodontics, with advances in instruments, materials, access design, irrigation systems, restoration materials, magnification, and digital technologies continuously shaping endodontic practice.1 However, as innovation accelerates, there emerges a growing apprehension that clinical decision making may shift from evidence-based principles toward commercial influence and the latest trends and techniques. At its core, the concern is no longer innovation itself but the gradual erosion of indication-based decision making when technological capability begins to influence whether treatment is performed, rather than how it is optimally delivered.
